title: Social Engineering Olympics — Final Debrief

fields.resolution: ENDEX. The facilitator stands and speaks clearly: 'This concludes the Social Engineering Olympics — Scenario 7. The exercise has ended. All teams, please set aside your role materials. We will now begin the debrief.'
finalState: The hidden threat was a coordinated social engineering campaign involving 9 attacks and 3 legitimate requests.
The exercise demonstrated the real-world tension between operational efficiency and security verification.
Teams were scored on correct identification of social engineering attempts and adherence to verification procedures.
The highest-scoring team will be awarded the gold medal for excellence in human factor awareness.
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. Put down your phones and radios. We will take ten minutes, then start the hot wash.
fields.hotWashMethod: 3-Up, 3-Down: three things that went well, three things that broke
hotWashQuestions: Which contact fooled you the most, and why?
Which legitimate contact did you almost reject — and what made it seem suspicious?
Which social engineering technique was hardest to spot — and why?
What would you change about your verification procedures after today?
How can we improve cross-team communication during a social engineering incident?
fields.facilitatorNote: Collect all ICS 201 forms and evaluator sheets before the break. Award gold medal to top-scoring team.

instructorNote: Score teams based on correct identification of social engineering vs. legitimate contacts. Award gold medal to the highest-scoring team.
